findings.cross_file_justification: .claude/adapters/tests/test_ceiling_e2e.py::test_calibration_exit_redacts_secret_shapes_in_the_recorded_message patches redact_payload_strings to identity and asserts the provider message is redacted at the field level; the diff passes str(_exc) through untouched, so the test's contract is not met by this code.
findings.description: The new calibration exit path stores the raw provider error text under `message_redacted` and prints it again verbatim via `_error_json(...)` to stderr. The text originates from the provider's HTTP 400/413 body (anthropic_adapter.py raises ProviderContextLimitError with f"HTTP {status} context-limit: {_msg}"). Provider error bodies can echo request fragments, and a misbehaving or proxied endpoint can return arbitrary text. Every other models_failed row in cheval uses a redacted message; this path skips the redaction helper despite the field name.
findings.failure_mode: A secret-shaped string (API key, bearer token) echoed in a provider 400 body lands unredacted in the MODELINV envelope (`models_failed[].message_redacted`) and in the operator stderr JSON log, where it is persisted and may be shipped to log aggregation.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `str(_exc)` through the same redaction helper used for the other models_failed rows (redact_payload_strings / the module-level redactor) before placing it in `message_redacted` and before building the `_error_json` message. Add the e2e test to CI if it is not already failing.

findings.cross_file_justification: anthropic_adapter.py (diff) raises ProviderContextLimitError for ANY 400/413 whose message matches is_context_limit_message and fills input_tokens/limit from parse_context_limit(_msg); cheval.py (diff) writes those provider-supplied integers into the persistent observed store via record_observed in routing/ceiling.py (omitted from this review), which then lowers the input bound for all later invocations (test_ceiling_e2e shows observed_for == limit+1 and the next call preempts).
findings.description: The self-correcting ceiling store is populated with numbers parsed out of a provider error message with no visible sanity floor or cross-check against the catalog. A single 400 response saying e.g. `prompt is too long: 100 tokens > 10 maximum` would record an observed bound of 11 and cause every subsequent request to that model to be preempted at the pre-flight gate until an operator runs the calibration probe. The trigger is any response body matching the context-limit regex, which includes legitimate but unrelated 400s (oversized tool description, system prompt limits) and anything returned by a proxy or misconfigured endpoint. The store path is also env-controlled (LOA_CHEVAL_CEILING_OBSERVED_PATH); ceiling.py's symlink/regular-file handling could not be verified because the file was omitted.
findings.failure_mode: Persistent self-inflicted denial of service for a model after one spurious or malicious context-limit error; the fallback chain is also bypassed because the error is deliberately non-walkable.
findings.suggested_fix: In record_observed / observed_for, reject observed values below a sane floor (e.g. the catalog's probed_ceiling / 4 or FLOOR_MAX_TOKENS) and above context_window, require `limit` and `input_tokens` to be mutually consistent (input > limit), ignore observations whose parsed limit is far below the catalog bound unless repeated N times, and give the store a TTL. Harden the store writer like ledger.py (realpath, O_NOFOLLOW, regular-file check). Tighten is_context_limit_message to the exact provider phrasing.

findings.cross_file_justification: test_ceiling_e2e.py::test_request_rate_429_while_unverified_walks_to_the_next_hop and ::test_unverified_status_is_per_hop_not_inherited_from_the_head encode the intended behaviour; the diff's RateLimitError branch checks only the head-level `_ceiling_unverified` flag and does not consult RateLimitError.token_limited.
findings.description: `_ceiling_unverified` is computed once from the head entry's pre-flight outcome and never reset per hop, and the RateLimitError short-circuit does not distinguish a token-limit 429 from a plain request-rate 429. Consequently, when the head ran above its probed bound and failed for a walkable reason, an ordinary rate-limit 429 on a calibrated fallback hop ends the invocation as RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED and appends a calibration record attributed to that hop.
findings.failure_mode: Fallback chain bypassed on transient rate limiting; spurious calibration_needed records written for hops that were never unverified; operators told to recalibrate the wrong model.
findings.suggested_fix: Track unverified status per hop (recompute from the hop's own input_bound decision) and only short-circuit when `getattr(_e, 'token_limited', False)` is True; otherwise fall through to the existing walk.

findings.description: The allowlist regex ends in `$`, and `re.match` with `$` also matches immediately before a trailing newline. A catalog value such as `context-1m-2025-08-07\n` passes the allowlist at `_beta_header_value` (line 174) and is joined into the `anthropic-beta` header value with a newline embedded. Both http.client and httpx reject such header values, so this is not currently exploitable for header injection, but the allowlist is weaker than documented and depends on the transport for safety.
findings.failure_mode: A YAML value with a trailing newline bypasses the allowlist and produces a transport-level ValueError (invalid header) instead of the intended ConfigError naming the entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `_BETA_HEADER_RE.fullmatch(item)` or terminate the pattern with `\Z` instead of `$`.

findings.description: The urllib fallback in the new `http_get` uses `urlopen`, which follows HTTP redirects by default and re-sends all request headers (including `x-api-key`) to the redirect target. The httpx branch does not follow redirects, so behaviour differs by installed client. The URL is the operator-configured endpoint plus `/models?limit=1`, so exploitation requires a redirecting proxy or a compromised endpoint, but the health probe is now the first call made against every configured provider.
findings.failure_mode: A 3xx from the configured endpoint (or an intermediary) causes the Anthropic API key to be forwarded to an arbitrary third-party host.
findings.suggested_fix: Install an opener with a redirect handler that refuses redirects (or strips auth headers), or treat any 3xx as a non-200 probe failure. Mirror whichever behaviour http_post already has.

findings.description: `_mult` accepts any value `float()` can parse and only rejects `<= 0`. YAML `.inf`, the string `"1e400"`, or `True` are accepted (inf > 0; bool → 1.0). An infinite multiplier makes `int(inp_cost * im)` in calculate_total_cost raise OverflowError, which fires inside create_ledger_entry after the billed provider call has completed.
findings.failure_mode: A malformed catalog multiplier turns every long-context call into an unhandled exception at ledger time, losing the cost row and the daily-spend update after money has been spent (budget enforcement blind spot).
findings.suggested_fix: Reject bool, NaN and non-finite values (`math.isfinite(m)`), and cap the multiplier to a sane range (e.g. 1.0 <= m <= 10.0); fall back to 1.0 and log a WARN on rejection.

findings.description: The new MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT generator interpolates the catalog model key `$m.key` into a bash `declare -A` literal without escaping. The value is type-checked as a number, but a key containing `"`, `$(`, or backticks would be emitted verbatim into generated-model-maps.sh, which is sourced by flatline-orchestrator.sh. This follows the pre-existing pattern of the other generated maps, so the exposure is not new, but the generator now has one more unescaped sink.
findings.failure_mode: A crafted model key in model-config.yaml executes arbitrary shell when the generated map is sourced.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate keys against `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$` in the jq filter (fail generation otherwise) or emit keys via `@sh` quoting.
